A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison; differences are confined to citations, bibliographic editing, and associated layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original continuous-control experiments, conversion-error analyses, CRPI evaluations, and energy estimates in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and analyses in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix B, including numerical MuJoCo and DeepMind Control results.

M1.justification: CRPI's residual-potential transfer, clipping, initialization, and inference procedure are unchanged in Section 5 and Algorithm 1. The neuron models and conversion procedures in Appendix A.3 also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four vector-observation MuJoCo environments and six visual DeepMind Control tasks. Appendix B.3 retains the same exclusion of Ant from DDPG results; no task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 and 9–11 retain the same comparisons involving ANN policies, IF, SNM, MT, DC, and the directly trained LIF, TC-LIF, and Spiking-WM methods. The two newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix A retain the same training budgets, architectures, simulation horizons, threshold settings, alpha search, and evaluation procedures. Ten rollout episodes per seed, the 1,000-step episode cap, and the reported performance metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The reward-decomposition and trajectory analyses, cross-step error correlations, alpha sensitivity curves, and membrane-potential initialization analysis are identical in Section 4, Figures 2–5, and Appendices B.1–B.2. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over five random seeds. The half-standard-deviation convention in Figure 3 and Tables 3 and 9–11 is retained, with no change to repeated-run information or statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains the IF, T=64 average performance ratios of 69.60% without CRPI and 91.84% with CRPI; no result entries are added or corrected.

T1.justification: The return decomposition, cosine-similarity definitions, residual-error assumptions, and CRPI derivation are unchanged. Equations 1–39, including the neuron dynamics in Appendix A.3, match between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about temporally correlated conversion errors, amplified state drift, and CRPI's training-free mitigation. The added introductory citations do not change these claims or their scope.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same mechanism interpretation, alpha overcorrection tradeoff, membrane-potential qualifications, and explanation for excluding DDPG Ant results. Applicability statements and proposed future extensions are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, architecture and preprocessing details in Appendix A, and deployment arithmetic and overhead information in Appendix B.4 are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds Song et al. (2026), SpikeVLA, and Li et al. (2026), Signal-adaptive trust regions for gradient-free optimization of recurrent spiking neural networks, to the introductory motivation and bibliography. This is a limited citation expansion without new positioning discussion or removal of existing works.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the added citations, changing Care-BN to CaRe-BN in the Xu et al. (2026b) reference, and updating the arXiv version/date stamp. The substantive prose and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added citations produce small spacing changes on page 1 and bibliography reflow across pages 11–13. Figure and table contents, captions, and structures are preserved; all other rendered pages, including the appendices, match.

improvement.justification: v3 slightly expands background citation coverage and corrects one reference's capitalization, but adds no explanatory discussion or scientific evidence. Methods, analyses, results, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so the editorial updates do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
